title: Miami Travel Guide

hero.headline: Miami Travel Guide
hero.subheadline: Build a Miami trip around distinct neighborhoods, Biscayne Bay, tropical gardens, and carefully planned excursions to South Florida's protected landscapes.

overview: Build a Miami trip around distinct neighborhoods, Biscayne Bay, tropical gardens, and carefully planned excursions to South Florida's protected landscapes.
Miami works best when Little Havana, Wynwood, Brickell, Coconut Grove, Miami Beach, and the Everglades are treated as different places rather than one generic downtown.

highlights.title: Miami essentials
highlights.description: Use the destination's defining landscapes, neighborhoods, and cultural sites to structure the visit.

highlights.title: Outdoor access
highlights.description: Build in time for the water, parks, preserves, or trails that genuinely define Miami.

highlights.title: Local context
highlights.description: Keep nearby municipalities and protected lands distinct so the itinerary stays geographically accurate.

highlights.title: Practical pacing
highlights.description: Group stops by area and leave room for weather, traffic, and seasonal conditions.

thingsToDo.title: Little Havana
thingsToDo.description: Walk Calle Ocho for Cuban-American food, music, bakeries, cigar shops, and Máximo Gómez Park; it is one of the clearest ways to understand modern Miami's immigrant history.

thingsToDo.title: Wynwood
thingsToDo.description: Explore the former warehouse district for large-scale murals, galleries, restaurants, and street art, then pair it with the nearby Design District if time allows.

thingsToDo.title: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
thingsToDo.description: Visit the early-20th-century Biscayne Bay estate for architecture, formal gardens, and a useful look at Miami before the modern skyline.

thingsToDo.title: Brickell and Downtown
thingsToDo.description: Combine Brickell's high-rise district with Downtown's bayfront and use Metromover to reduce short car trips.

thingsToDo.title: South Beach — in the separate City of Miami Beach
thingsToDo.description: Cross Biscayne Bay for the Art Deco Historic District, Ocean Drive, Lummus Park, and the Atlantic beach. South Beach is not inside the City of Miami.

thingsToDo.title: Everglades National Park day trip
thingsToDo.description: Plan the Everglades as a dedicated excursion to a separate National Park Service unit; it is a regional protected landscape, not a Miami city park.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

travelTips: Group each day by geography instead of crossing the region repeatedly.
Use early mornings for exposed outdoor activities and waterfront time.
Check park, marine, and weather conditions before nature-focused plans.
Treat nearby municipalities and protected areas as separate destinations with their own access rules.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Miami?
faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.q: Is Miami good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.
It depends on the destination, but a car or guided tour is often useful for protected lands and regional excursions.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For high-demand wildlife, boating, park, and holiday-period experiences, advance booking is sensible.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Miami is a mainland South Florida city shaped by immigration, finance, arts, food, and Biscayne Bay.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The city occupies the coastal plain along Biscayne Bay; Miami Beach sits on barrier islands as a separate municipality.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Cuban, Caribbean, Latin American, and global influences are central to Miami's neighborhoods and food culture.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Biscayne Bay supports boating and paddling, while Everglades and Biscayne national parks provide major protected landscapes outside the municipality.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Metromover works well in the urban core; rideshare, rental cars, or tours are useful for cross-bay and regional trips.
